summary: Everyday gadget curiosities and physical design mysteries like phone battery hazards, SIM card notches, and airplane window shapes drove the strongest view velocity. Conversely, generic kitchen science facts and abstract cosmic 'What If' scenarios consistently failed to generate traction. Moving forward, center all scripts around tangible tech hardware and ubiquitous everyday objects, weaving in a direct engagement question before executing the seamless end-to-beginning loop.
do_more: Focus on physical hardware mysteries of everyday gadgets like smartphone batteries, touchscreens, and SIM cards
Deconstruct non-intuitive design features of modern travel and tech objects like airplane windows and QR codes
Include a quick opinion or guess prompt right before the loop to convert passive viewers into commenters
avoid: Avoid textbook kitchen science topics like onion tears, boiling milk, or microwave radiation
Avoid abstract hypothetical space scenarios like the moon or ozone layer disappearing
Avoid dry historical anecdotes that lack modern hardware or software relevance
Avoid slow cinematic introductions; never spend more than 1.5 seconds introducing the core mystery
hook_tips: Highlight an immediate physical danger: 'Agar aapke phone ki battery me galti se chhed ho jaye, toh kya blast hoga?'
Point out a bizarre design detail hiding in plain sight: 'Notice kiya hai? Airplane ki windows hamesha round kyu hoti hain?'
Expose a common modern misconception: 'Expiry date paani ki nahi hoti, balki us plastic bottle ki hoti hai!'
State the surprising answer first, then explain: 'Aapka touchscreen ungli se chalta hai, par pencil se kyu nahi?'
title_tips: Use crisp curiosity tags at the end like '| 3 Quick Facts #Shorts' or 'Reality Check #Shorts'
Highlight everyday tech features: 'Airplane Window Round Kyu Hoti Hai? #Shorts'
Keep title lengths strictly under 55 characters so the core mystery is never cut off on mobile devices
